title: Times tables 2–12
blurb: One mnemonic per table, then a puzzle to fill the blanks yourself.

steps: Add it to itself (or skip-count by 2).
t2.exception: Doubling is ×2, not ×4. ×4 needs two doubles. And 0 × 2 is still 0.

t3.phrase: Double it, then add one more group.
steps: Double the other number first (that is ×2).
Add one more copy of that number.
t3.exception: Do not stop after the double — that is only ×2. And 3 × 3 is 9, not 6.

t4.exception: Count the doubles: one double is ×2, two doubles are ×4, three are ×8. Stopping early gives half the answer.

t5.phrase: Fives are half of tens — and they end in 0 or 5.
steps: Multiply by 10: stick a zero on the end.
Take half of that tens answer.
Check: even ×5 ends in 0; odd ×5 ends in 5.
t5.exception: If your answer ends in anything other than 0 or 5, it is wrong. Half of the tens product, not half of the other factor alone.

t6.phrase: Six is five plus one more group.
steps: Add one more copy of the other number.
t6.exception: Do not forget to add the extra group after ×5. And 6 × 6 is 36 (“magic tricks”), not 30.

t7.phrase: Five, six, seven, eight: fifty-six is seven times eight.
steps: Use the famous rhymes for the hard facts (7×7, 7×8).
For other factors, build from a fact you know: 7 × 6 is 7 × 5 plus 7.
t7.exception: A rhyme is a hook, not the reason. If you forget it, use 7 × 7 = 49 and add or take away sevens. 7 × 0 is 0.

t8.exception: Three doubles, not two — stopping at ×4 is half of ×8. Hard square: “I ate and ate and got sick on the floor: eight times eight is sixty-four.”

t9.phrase: Fold the finger. Digits always add to nine.
steps: For 9 × n, fold down finger n.
Fingers on the left are tens; fingers on the right are ones. Check: the two digits sum to 9.
t9.exception: Fingers work for 9 × 1 through 9 × 10. For 9 × 11 or 9 × 12, do 10 × that number and subtract it. 9 × 0 is 0.

t10.phrase: Times ten: stick a zero on the end.
steps: Put a zero on the end.
t10.exception: Sticking a zero is ×10, not ×100 (that needs two zeros). And 10 × 0 is 0, not 10.

t11.phrase: One digit: write it twice. Two digits: split and park the sum.
steps: For a two-digit number: split the digits, add them, park the sum in the middle.
t11.exception: If the middle sum is 10 or more, carry 1 to the left digit. Beyond two digits the same idea needs place-value carrying. 11 × 11 = 121; 11 × 12 = 132.

t12.phrase: Twelve is ten plus two: ×10, then add a double.
steps: Find ×10: stick a zero on the end.
t12.exception: Add ×10 and ×2 — do not multiply them together. 12 × 12 is 144 (“one forty-four”), not 120 + 12.
